'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]], [[Bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
***Israeli airstrikes kill at least 24 people in [[Gaza City]], including ten family members of [[Hamas]] political chief [[Ismail Haniyeh]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-airstrikes-kill-least-24-gaza-city-say-gaza-officials-2024-06-25/ (Reuters)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/25/israeli-air-strike-kills-10-family-members-of-hamas-chief-haniyeh-in-gaza (Al Jazeera)] 
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**The [[European Court of Human Rights]] unanimously finds [[Russia]] guilty of systematic violations of [[human rights]] in the [[Crimean peninsula]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/6/25/top-european-court-finds-russia-guilty-of-rights-violations-in-crimea (Al Jazeera)]
**Russia and [[Ukraine]] each return 90 prisoners of war in a [[prisoner exchange]] mediated by the [[United Arab Emirates]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-ukraine-each-return-90-prisoners-war-russian-defence-ministry-says-2024-06-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Haitian crisis (2018–present)|Haitian crisis]]
**[[Kenya]]n police units arrive in [[Haiti]] for a [[United Nations]]-backed [[Multinational Security Support Mission in Haiti|security mission]] to restore order. [https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20240625-kenyan-police-force-arrives-haiti-un-backed-security-mission (France 24)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2024/06/25/kenya-haiti-security-force/ (''The Washington Post'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[European Commission]] levies an [[antitrust]] fine against [[Microsoft]], charging it with violating [[European Union competition law]] by illegally linking its [[Microsoft Teams]] app with [[Microsoft Office]], giving the former an unfair advantage over [[Slack (software)|Slack]]. [https://www.reuters.com/technology/eu-charges-microsoft-with-abusive-bundling-teams-with-office-2024-06-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 North America heat waves]]
**[[Puerto Rico]] announces its first island-wide [[heat advisory]] to all 78 municipalities due to predicted highs of 114°F (46°C) and widespread [[power outage]]s. [https://apnews.com/article/puerto-rico-heat-advisory-46a70c2341d74f9ccdf03a5d83e3dc91 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Enlargement of the European Union]]
**[[Accession of Ukraine to the European Union]], [[Accession of Moldova to the European Union]]
***The [[European Union]] formally launches accession negotiations with [[Ukraine]] and [[Moldova]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/eu-kicks-off-membership-talks-with-ukraine-moldova-19679ac6 (''Barron's'')]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Department of the Treasury]] announces [[economic sanctions]] on 50 people and companies in [[Hong Kong]], the [[United Arab Emirates]], and the [[Marshall Islands]], for allegedly funding and helping [[Iran's military]] gain access to the international financial system. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2024/6/25/us-sanctions-sprawling-shadow-banking-network-that-helps-irans-military (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe]] elects former [[Switzerland|Swiss]] president [[Alain Berset]] as the [[Council of Europe|Council]]'s new Secretary General, succeeding [[Marija Pejčinović Burić]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/new-secretary-general-elected-to-lead-council-of-europe/ (Politico)]
*[[Russia]] bans 81 media outlets from access inside the country, including [[Agence France-Presse]] and [[Politico]], in retaliation for a [[European Union]] ban on [[Mass media in Russia|Russian media outlets]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russia-bans-distribution-dozens-eu-news-outlets-retaliatory-step-2024-06-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Gun violence in the United States]]
**[[U.S. Surgeon General]] [[Vivek Murthy]] declares [[gun violence]] a [[public health emergency (United States)|public health emergency]]. [https://apnews.com/article/surgeon-general-gun-control-violence-deaths-murthy-24b53f1aaace068e0cb24ae809853f66 (AP)]
**A gunman kills five people and critically injures a girl in [[North Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], then kills himself upon being confronted by [[Las Vegas Police Department|the police]] the following day. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/five-dead-las-vegas-shooting-suspect-arrested-local-media-reports-2024-06-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Conscription of yeshiva students]]
**The [[Supreme Court of Israel]] rules that the [[Israel Defense Forces]] and the [[Government of Israel|government]] are legally bound to [[Conscription|conscript]] [[Haredi Judaism|Haredi]] [[yeshiva]] students, overturning their prior [[Exemption from military service in Israel|exemption]] from [[Conscription in Israel|mandatory military service]]. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-807625 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.npr.org/2024/06/25/g-s1-6116/israeli-supreme-court-rules-that-the-military-must-begin-drafting-ultra-orthodox-men (NPR)]
*[[Indictment and arrest of Julian Assange]]
**[[WikiLeaks]] founder [[Julian Assange]] is freed following a plea deal with the [[United States]], which results in Assange pleading guilty to [[espionage]]-related charges. [https://www.reuters.com/world/wikileaks-julian-assange-set-be-freed-after-pleading-guilty-us-espionage-charge-2024-06-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[International Criminal Court investigation in Ukraine]]
**The [[International Criminal Court]] issues arrest warrants for [[Russia]]'s [[Chief of the General Staff (Russia)|Chief of the General Staff]] [[Valery Gerasimov]] and former [[Minister of Defence (Russia)|defence minister]] [[Sergei Shoigu]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/icc-issues-arrest-warrants-for-russia-army-chief-ex-minister-26e03854 (''Barron's'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/25/icc-issues-arrest-warrants-for-russias-sergei-shoigu-and-valery-gerasimov (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Kenya Finance Bill protests]]
**[[2024 Parliament of Kenya assault]]
***Thousands of anti-tax protestors assault and set the [[Parliament of Kenya]] building in [[Nairobi]] [[Arson|on fire]], as riots begin following the approval of a finance bill. The ceremonial mace is also stolen by protesters. Ten people are killed and more than 50 others are injured as police open fire on protestors. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/6/25/kenya-protests-live-deadly-anti-tax-protests-after-finance-bill-approved (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cerrv93yx1mo (BBC News)]
***[[Kenyan President|President]] [[William Ruto]] deploys the [[Kenya Defence Forces|military]] to stop the protests. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-06-25/kenyan-president-deploys-military-to-halt-treasonous-protests (Bloomberg)]
*[[2024 United Kingdom general election date betting scandal]]
**A fifth [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] member is investigated for involvement in the ongoing election betting scandal. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/article/2024/jun/25/election-betting-fifth-tory-investigated-in-growing-scandal (''The Guardian'')]
*[[LGBT rights in Peru]]
**The [[Peru]]vian [[Ministry of Health (Peru)|Ministry of Health]] announces that it will stop labeling [[transgender]] individuals as suffering from [[mental disorder]]s, but will instead use the term "[[gender dysphoria|gender discordance]]". [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-stop-labeling-transgender-people-mentally-ill-2024-06-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Spanish General Council of the Judiciary blockade]]
**The two major political parties, [[Spanish Socialist Workers' Party]] and [[People's Party (Spain)|People's Party]] agree to renew the members of the [[General Council of the Judiciary]] after five years of blockade and the necessary mediation by the [[European Commission]] to reach an agreement. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/spain%27s-main-parties-agree-to-renew-judges%27-governing-body-after-five-year-deadlock/81784241 (''SWI'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Chinese space program]]
**The [[Chang'e 6]] lunar exploration mission successfully returns to Earth after collecting [[lunar rock|rock]] and [[lunar soil|soil]] samples from the [[far side of the Moon]]. [https://apnews.com/article/china-far-side-of-moon-probe-samples-c2dd59505402c07f9382bbca14eed4cf (AP)]
